intakeRunbook.name: Creating IcM incidents for DDFun customer requests

fallbackPlaybook.name: DDFun customer request intake
fallbackPlaybook.selection: Fallback: no specific vendor playbook matched the Teams message.
remediationGuidance: Investigate the reported issue using the evidence in the originating Teams thread.
Record the remediation or final disposition in the IcM.
validationCriteria: Confirm the reported customer impact is mitigated.
Document the completed remediation or disposition before resolving the IcM.

playbooks.name: Reimaging On-Prem Machines
playbooks.selection: Matched reimaging or fresh-OS-installation language for an on-prem Helix machine.
remediationGuidance: Confirm the exact machine and queue names, then take the machine offline with the OSOB CLI or Swagger API before touching it.
Reimage over KVM, reinstall the Helix client, and reinstall the queue-specific software the queue requires.
Bring the machine back online only after the client is installed and configured for its queue.
validationCriteria: Confirm the machine heartbeats and picks up work in the Grafana queue monitor.
Confirm test work items complete successfully on the machine before closing.

playbooks.name: Onboarding Spare or New Hardware into Helix
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to deploy approved spare or new physical hardware into a Helix on-prem queue.
remediationGuidance: Accept the deployment packet and confirm the asset, hostname, queue, environment, and security boundary match the approved work item.
Rack, image, and secure the host, create exactly one inventory record mapping it to one queue, and quarantine it with the local offline marker before bootstrap.
Bootstrap the approved Azure Arc or OneCert path, apply queue-specific configuration, and remove temporary credentials.
validationCriteria: Confirm a fresh heartbeat under the exact queue and machine identity while the host is still quarantined.
Confirm a representative Helix work item ran, finished, and uploaded logs, plus performance or tethered-device validation where applicable.
Confirm the requester and the DNCEng DRI recorded acceptance in the work item before close-out.

playbooks.name: Onboarding Helix Machines with Azure Arc
playbooks.selection: Matched Azure Arc onboarding language for a Windows x64 or Arc-supported Linux Helix machine.
remediationGuidance: Confirm the work item assigns the Arc authentication path; use the OneCert playbook for macOS, Windows ARM64, Alpine, or Raspbian instead of inferring from the queue name.
Connect the machine to Azure Arc with the approved service principal, subscription, and resource group, then create MachineSetting.json with the approved FederatedClientID.
Keep the machine disabled in Helix until every verification step passes.
validationCriteria: Confirm the Arc resource reports Connected and its name, subscription, and resource group match the approved work item.
Confirm a fresh Helix heartbeat in the expected queue and a representative work item that completes and uploads logs.
Record the Arc resource ID, queue, heartbeat time, and work-item result without any certificate or private-key material.

playbooks.name: Onboarding Helix Machines with OneCert
playbooks.selection: Matched certificate-based (OneCert) Helix onboarding language for a clean Windows, Linux, or macOS machine.
remediationGuidance: Confirm the target environment, queue, service principal, and certificate version with the work-item owner before starting.
Create the helix-prep directory, place the onboarding certificate, and run the bootstrap script with the approved parameters.
Remove the temporary certificate during post-installation cleanup and keep the machine disabled in Helix until verification passes.
validationCriteria: Confirm a fresh Helix heartbeat in the expected queue.
Confirm a representative Helix work item completes and uploads its logs, then enable the machine.
Record the queue, heartbeat time, work-item result, certificate name and version, and operator, without certificate contents.

playbooks.name: Upgrading OS on Helix Queue Devices
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to upgrade the operating system on physical devices backing a Helix queue.
remediationGuidance: Plan and obtain approval first, and create the replacement queue when the new OS version needs its own queue name.
Upgrade one machine at a time: take it offline, upgrade over KVM or SSH, then reinstall queue-specific tooling such as the required Xcode version.
Re-pair tethered iOS or tvOS devices after a macOS upgrade, and remove the old queue once the migration is complete.
validationCriteria: Confirm each upgraded machine heartbeats and completes work items on the target queue.
Confirm EstimatedRemovalDate and UpdateRequiredDate were updated in the queue definition, and the Matrix of Truth where applicable.

playbooks.name: Updating OS EOL Dates in Helix
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to set or correct Helix queue or image lifecycle dates.
remediationGuidance: Determine the authoritative EOL date from the OS publisher, or an earlier date when DNCEng has reason to remove sooner.
Update EstimatedRemovalDate and UpdateRequiredDate in the queue or image YAML in dotnet-helix-machines, with a comment citing the source and updater.
Open a PR listing the affected queues, the source of the EOL information, and the work item.
validationCriteria: Confirm the dotnet-helix-machines-ci pipeline builds successfully with the date warnings or errors cleared.
Confirm the Matrix of Truth data source reflects the new dates when it is in scope.

playbooks.name: Decommissioning On-Prem Devices
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to permanently retire physical on-prem hardware from Helix service.
remediationGuidance: Inventory the exact devices and prove no active dependency remains; deprecate the queue first if product teams still use it.
Take each device offline, remove its Helix queue registration, and wipe credentials, certificates, and residual test data.
File a DDFun IcM for the physical removal listing machine names, locations, and whether the hardware is stored, repurposed, or disposed of.
validationCriteria: Confirm the decommissioned machines no longer appear in the queue or heartbeat data.
Confirm the work item records the machine list, decommission date, and the IcM reference for physical removal.

playbooks.name: Deprecating and Removing Helix Queues
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to deprecate or remove a Helix queue from service.
remediationGuidance: Assess recent queue usage, obtain removal approval, and communicate the deprecation to consumers before changing anything.
Open a PR removing the queue definition from dotnet-helix-machines, plus any custom image definition no longer referenced.
Take on-prem machines offline before the removal PR merges, and let the autoscaler clean up VM scale sets for cloud queues.
validationCriteria: Confirm the dotnet-helix-machines-ci build succeeds and the queue no longer appears on helix.dot.net.
Confirm stale HeartBeat and OsobInventory rows are deleted and any queue-specific dashboards, alerts, and Azure resources are cleaned up.

playbooks.name: Managing On-Prem Machine Passwords
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to audit, strengthen, or rotate passwords on on-prem Helix machines.
remediationGuidance: Audit current passwords and identify any shared between internal and open queue machines, which must differ.
Generate strong per-boundary passwords, take each machine offline, and apply the change over KVM or SSH.
Store the new values in Key Vault, update every automation, script, and KVM reference, and notify DDFun of the change.
validationCriteria: Confirm each machine is reachable with the new credential and back online processing work.
Confirm no stale password remains in Key Vault, repo content, or DDFun records, and that internal and open queues no longer share a password.

playbooks.name: Bringing On-Prem Machines Back Online
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to restore an existing on-prem machine to active service in its Helix queue.
remediationGuidance: Confirm the machine is powered on and reachable over KVM or SSH, contacting DDFun for physical state if it is not.
Check the machine state through the Helix API and determine whether it is disabled via API, blocked by an offline file, or not communicating.
Resolve the underlying fault, remove the offline file or re-enable the machine, and restart the Helix client.
validationCriteria: Confirm a heartbeat appears within 5-10 minutes in the Grafana queue monitor or the helixscripts2 HeartBeat table.
Confirm work items are assigned and complete successfully, sending a test job on a low-traffic queue if needed.
Monitor at least 30 minutes of stable operation before closing.

playbooks.name: Creating Azure DevOps Pipelines
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to create a YAML pipeline in dnceng/internal or dnceng-public/public.
remediationGuidance: Require the exact project, pipeline name and folder, source repository, committed YAML path and ref, Service Tree service, production classification, agent pool, protected resources, and validation owner.
Create the definition without its first run, apply the customer-provided StartRight classification, and authorize only the approved resources for that pipeline.
Do not create customer YAML, grant signing, approve a new internal-to-GitHub connection, or weaken checks and approvals as part of pipeline creation.
validationCriteria: Confirm the pipeline name, project, repository, YAML path, production classification, and Service Tree ownership match the request.
Confirm a representative customer run uses the intended pool and only the expected protected resources.
Record the pipeline and validation-build URLs plus the customer's confirmation before closing.

playbooks.name: Retiring Azure DevOps Repositories and Pipelines
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to disable, archive, or delete an Azure Repos Git repository or YAML/build pipeline.
remediationGuidance: Require the exact resources, owning team, DRI-approved retirement mode, completed dependency inventory, and observation end timestamp before acting.
Activate PIM, recheck pipeline consumers, then disable first and observe the staged state for the approved window.
Only then archive or delete, recording rollback data and the 30-day repository recovery deadline.
validationCriteria: Confirm names and immutable IDs match the approved tracking item and the dependency inventory has no unknown consumers.
Confirm the staged states completed their observation windows without impact and the replacement passed customer validation.
Confirm the PIM assignment is deactivated and all owners are recorded in the system of record.

playbooks.name: Granting Azure DevOps Access and Permissions
playbooks.selection: Matched a least-privilege access request for an existing Azure DevOps repository, pipeline, branch, feed, or agent pool.
remediationGuidance: Validate that the resource exists and the request is not for administrator, feed owner, manage-permissions, policy-bypass, or force-push capability.
Activate PIM and add only the least-privilege permission or role to the approved group for the named resource.
Do not change inheritance, owner, or administrator permissions; route service connection, signing, secret, and variable-group requests elsewhere.
validationCriteria: Confirm a representative customer completed the real operation successfully; a permission page showing Allow is not sufficient.
Confirm the tracking item records the previous and changed states, validation evidence, owner, and any next action.

playbooks.name: Preparing .NET Engineering Services Rollout Pull Requests
playbooks.selection: Matched a rollout-preparation request for dotnet-helix-machines, dotnet-helix-service, or dotnet/dnceng.
remediationGuidance: Treat the IcM's repository scope and requested date as authoritative; do not add a repository or infer a date from cadence.
Determine which repositories have changes, select an eligible cutoff commit, and create the rollout branch and PR for each.
Build and review release notes, record staging evidence, and hand the IcM to the named DNCEng owner.
validationCriteria: Confirm every repository in the IcM is explicitly marked No rollout, Prepared, or Deferred with its cutoff, PR, CI build, and staging result recorded.
Confirm release notes match the final rollout PRs and that unresolved warnings, failed policies, and missing reviewers are recorded.
Confirm DDFun has not merged a rollout PR, approved a production gate, or executed a production deployment.

playbooks.name: Creating On-Prem Queues
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to create a Helix queue backed by physical hardware such as perf or tethered device machines.
remediationGuidance: Determine the queue properties, including name, OperatingSystemId, and machine set, from the requesting work item.
Add the queue definition to the appropriate file under definitions/ in dotnet-helix-machines.
Open a PR that names the queues, references the work item, and obtain DNCEng review before rollout.
validationCriteria: Confirm the pipeline processes the definition without YAML, duplicate-name, or OperatingSystemId errors.
Confirm a FORCE_QUEUE test job is picked up and completed by the physical machines.
Confirm the queue appears on helix.dot.net after merge and that stakeholders were notified.

playbooks.name: Creating VS Queues
playbooks.selection: Matched a request for Visual Studio build and test queues on 1ES Hosted Pools.
remediationGuidance: Add the version anchor and image definition to definition-base/windows.base.yaml, then the four build and test queues to definitions/shared/windows.yaml.
Handle VS activation, and update artifacts/windows-vs-workloads only when new workloads are required.
Open a PR listing the VS version and SKU, all queue names, the base Windows Server image, and any new vault secrets.
validationCriteria: Confirm the pipeline processes the definitions without YAML, missing base image, or vault reference errors.
Confirm a build targeting the new queue shows Visual Studio installed at the expected version with the expected workloads present.

playbooks.name: Creating Cloud / VM-based Helix Queues
playbooks.selection: Matched a request for an Azure VM-backed Helix test queue on an OS and image Helix already supports.
remediationGuidance: Confirm an existing queue already uses the target OperatingSystemId, image, and architecture; otherwise route the request to the new OS/SKU onboarding playbook first.
Verify the VM SKU and regional quota, copy a template queue, reuse the image reference and artifact group, and create the Standard and Open pair plus any subscription variants.
Set OperatingSystemId, AzureComputeUnit/MinCores, and lifecycle dates, and keep queue names within 42 characters.
validationCriteria: Confirm Types.Tests, DeployQueues.Tests, and the Validate tool pass locally after Build.cmd.
Confirm a test deployment produces working queues and that every new queue resolves to ProtectedMode.Mode: Off with no wait threshold.
Confirm the SKU and quota verification record is Pass and is linked from the work item.

playbooks.name: Creating & Managing 1ES Hosted Pools
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to create or reconfigure a 1ES Hosted Pool that backs DNCEng CI/CD builds.
remediationGuidance: Confirm the requirements, then create the pool through 1ES Hub in its mapped production subscription and validate capacity.
Add the pool definition to definitions/shared/hostedpools.yaml, plus overflow load balancing and pipeline wiring only when required.
If the initial deployment needs quota, open a tracking work item, record the quota-granted mail, and redeploy with the final settings.
validationCriteria: Confirm dotnet test test/Types.Tests/ and test/Deploy1ESHostedPools.Tests/ pass.
Confirm the pool exists in its dedicated resource group with the final name, region, VM SKU, visibility, and maximum size.
Confirm a scale-out smoke test reached Scaling.Production.MaximumSize concurrently running agents and the evidence is in the work item.

playbooks.name: Making an Existing Azure Subscription Ready for Helix Queues
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to make an existing, enabled Azure subscription ready to host production Helix queues.
remediationGuidance: Confirm the subscription exists, reports Enabled, and that the proposed logical route is absent from main in dotnet-helix-machines.
Register the required resource providers, confirm VM-family quota per region, and plan target-subscription RBAC within the documented boundary.
Add the case-sensitive logical route in dotnet-helix-machines and the core limit in dotnet-autoscaler, merging both just in time.
validationCriteria: Confirm every required provider reports Registered; Registering and NotRegistered do not qualify.
Confirm the VM family and regional quota meet the approved core requirement and every required RBAC assignment is verified at its scope.
Confirm the DNCEng DRI approval is recorded in the queue-request IcM before handoff.

playbooks.name: Service Connection Remediation
playbooks.selection: Matched a pipeline failure involving an Azure DevOps service connection, WIF, or feed authentication.
remediationGuidance: Use the symptom decision table to isolate the failing boundary: connection lookup, pipeline authorization, federated credential, Azure resource authorization, NuGet authentication, or network access.
Do not assume every 403 is an identity problem; network ACLs, firewalls, and resource policy can deny an already authenticated caller.
Apply the least-privilege fix and do not broaden an identity, bypass pipeline checks, or change a customer-owned identity without owner approval.
validationCriteria: Confirm a representative pipeline run on the operative branch resolves the connection without an interactive permit prompt and acquires a token.
Confirm the original target operation succeeds and, for a replacement connection, verify a post-merge or production-branch run.
Confirm the customer validated the workload; keep a follow-up open if service was restored with temporary or legacy credentials.

playbooks.name: Onboarding a New OS, OS Version, or Azure VM SKU to Helix
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to onboard an operating system, OS version, or Azure VM SKU that Helix does not yet offer.
remediationGuidance: Run the guided onboarding wizard to pick the path and record the result; if the OS, image, and VM capability already exist, use the cloud queue playbook instead.
Provide the image first, either a pinned marketplace image or a base-images definition, then author the Standard and Open queue definitions.
Derive OperatingSystemId from the neighboring {OS}-{Distro}-{Version}-{Arch} convention and set lifecycle dates, defaulting EstimatedRemovalDate to five years out when no authoritative date exists.
validationCriteria: Confirm BaseImages.Tests, Types.Tests, and DeployQueues.Tests pass, and that Image Generation completed on the branch before the PR pipeline re-ran.
Confirm a custom image build and test deployment succeed and every new queue resolves to ProtectedMode.Mode: Off.
Confirm the requesting team's workload passed on every new production queue.

playbooks.name: Performing Recurring Helix Artifact Maintenance
playbooks.selection: Matched recurring artifact UpdateDate warnings from a dotnet-helix-machines build.
remediationGuidance: Start when the warning first appears, 21 days before UpdateDate, rather than waiting for it to become a build error.
Classify every warning with an owner, then process one artifact at a time on a clean feature branch using that artifact's README instructions.
Update lifecycle dates, record the affected-lineage and rollback matrices, and roll out the merged change with any required pin PR.
validationCriteria: Confirm release provenance and integrity checks passed and every edit and lifecycle date is approved and consistent.
Confirm staging and production use the intended images and that existing active instances no longer run the old image.
Confirm representative requester workloads pass, the observation window completes, and temporary payloads and elevation are removed.

playbooks.name: Changing Helix Queue Artifacts and Images
playbooks.selection: Matched a change to artifacts, base images, or pinned gallery images on gallery-backed Helix queues.
remediationGuidance: Classify the change and build the complete image-lineage and queue impact matrix, handling legacy or non-reproducible images explicitly.
Merge the source PR, rebuild every affected reproducible image, record the exact gallery versions, and update every GalleryImageVersion pin in a follow-up PR.
Validate staging, promote to HelixImagesProd, deploy production, then update existing VMSS instances so running machines pick up the new image.
validationCriteria: Confirm each affected image was built from the expected commit and its exact gallery version is recorded.
Confirm the staging deployment and the requester workload passed before production promotion.
Verify from the consumer's perspective after deployment and complete the observation window before close-out.

playbooks.name: Updating Visual Studio 2022 Helix Images
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to update the Visual Studio 2022 version and installation source used by Helix Windows images.
remediationGuidance: Determine the target Release or Preview version from the VS 2022 schedule and official release data, then update every affected version and permanent installation URL in base-images/variables.json.
Generate and verify every golden layer from the feature branch, recording each tracking ID and exact replicated gallery destination.
Pin the exact golden-layer names and versions in definition-base/windows.base.yaml and merge one PR containing both the source and pin updates.
validationCriteria: Confirm every Image Factory job succeeded and replication completed with a recorded gallery, image name, and version.
Confirm the schedule, variables, image pins, and generated images all agree.
Confirm the main dotnet-helix-machines CI Build Images phase succeeds for every affected VS 2022 lineage.

playbooks.name: Updating Visual Studio 2026 Helix Images
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to update the Visual Studio 2026 version and installation source used by Helix Windows images.
remediationGuidance: Determine the target Release or Insiders version from the VS 2026 schedule and official release data, then update every affected version and permanent installation URL in base-images/variables.json.
Generate and verify every golden layer from the feature branch, recording each tracking ID and exact replicated gallery destination.
Pin the exact golden-layer names and versions in definition-base/windows.base.yaml and merge one PR containing both the source and pin updates.
validationCriteria: Confirm every Image Factory job succeeded and replication completed with a recorded gallery, image name, and version.
Confirm the schedule, variables, image pins, and generated images all agree.
Confirm the main dotnet-helix-machines CI Build Images phase succeeds for every affected VS 2026 lineage.

playbooks.name: Apple Account Migration
playbooks.selection: Matched a request about the shared Apple Developer account used to sign and run .NET tests on Helix Apple devices.
remediationGuidance: Determine the migration path for the shared Apple Developer account and complete the pre-migration checklist before changing anything.
Execute the migration to a Microsoft-managed Apple Account, then re-establish 2FA for the Apple Developer Portal.
Regenerate signing certificates and provisioning profiles only if signing fails after the migration.
validationCriteria: Confirm portal access to Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles, that all devices remain registered, that profiles remain valid, and that the program membership is active.
Confirm the xharness pipeline Apple device E2E tests install applications successfully.

playbooks.name: Manual Rotation of a domain-account Using secret-manager
matchTerms: user intervention required for creation or rotation of a domain account
playbooks.selection: Matched a secret-rotation build requiring manual rotation of an existing domain-account.
remediationGuidance: Confirm the failed manifest entry is a domain-account and record its exact secret name and accountName; do not use this playbook for another manual secret type.
Run secret-manager interactively in a private, unrecorded terminal, reset the account password in CoreIdentity, and enter that exact generated value into the waiting prompt.
Keep CoreIdentity and Key Vault synchronized, clear the clipboard afterward, and never copy the old or new password into the IcM.
validationCriteria: Confirm secret-manager reports the exact secret as Rotated and exits without an error.
Confirm any required account extension was completed and record only the account and secret names, never secret values.
Have the DNCEng DRI confirm correct consumer operation before closing the IcM.

playbooks.name: Manual Rotation of a github-app-secret Using secret-manager
matchTerms: user intervention required for creation or rotation of github app secret
playbooks.selection: Matched a secret-rotation build requiring manual rotation of an existing github-app-secret.
remediationGuidance: Confirm the manifest entry is an existing github-app-secret, identify the owning GitHub App, Key Vault, enabled credential components, and consumer validation plan before generating anything.
Run secret-manager interactively and rotate only the private key, OAuth client secret, or webhook secret required by the manifest and coordinated plan.
Keep old GitHub credentials active until the DNCEng DRI restarts and validates every consumer; never record credentials, private-key contents, or local PEM paths.
validationCriteria: Confirm secret-manager reports successful storage for the exact composite secret and delete the downloaded PEM after storage succeeds.
Confirm every consuming service authenticates as the GitHub App and processes webhooks where applicable after its restart.
Remove old GitHub credentials only after consumer validation, then record the rotated components without secret material.

playbooks.name: Releasing Quarantined Packages
playbooks.selection: Matched a request to release a package version before its seven-day Azure Artifacts quarantine expires.
remediationGuidance: Require the target feed, package name, exact version, business justification, and requesting contact, and decline routine or Dependabot upgrades.
Release packages destined for dotnet-public from the dotnet-public-intermediate feed in dnceng/internal, not from dotnet-public.
On the Upstream Versions tab, confirm the version still shows as quarantined, then use Release from Quarantine and enter the business justification.
validationCriteria: Confirm the released feed, package name, and exact version are recorded in the IcM.
Confirm the customer's build succeeded or they can access the package before resolving.
